newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Beef scare hits Belgian fast-food chain profit.
newsitem.headline: Beef scare hits Belgian fast-food chain profit.

text.p: Belgian fast-food chain Quick Restaurants SA said on Monday the British beef scare sent its first half 1996 profits tumbling and that it expected a 30 to 35 percent fall in net profit for the year as a whole.
"The mad-cow crisis caused a violent drop in the number of people visiting restaurants...on all the markets where Quick is present," the company said in a statement.

"This phenomenon has been amplified by the difficult economic context and by the (general) slowdown in consumption levels," it added. The company had already announced in July that full year 1996 profits would be below 1995 levels.
First half consolidated net profit plunged to seven million francs from 147 million in same period last year. Turnover totalled 10.35 billion versus 9.26 billion.

Quick reiterated its forecast made in July of a 10 to 12 percent rise in sales for the full year -- before then the company had been forecasting a 15 percent increase. Quick plans to open 60 new restaurants in the year as a whole.
Quick, which said it was always able to certify the quality and origin of the beef served in its restaurants, believed consumers' fears about beef should progressively diminish.
"With the fast food market retaining all its potential for development, Quick expects to re-discover a more sustained rhythm of growth from 1997," the statement said.
